thread:
Naomi Feldman: Hey all — need security sign-off on the *outbound* fields for PLG→Sales signals before we turn on HubSpot writes + Slack pings. Can you review proposed payload + call out any PII/data-minimization issues?

Naomi Feldman: Proposed event (v1) is account-level only, but I want to sanity check before we lock the schema.

Naomi Feldman: Draft payload (to HubSpot timeline event; Slack message is a subset):
```
{
  event_type: "plg_signal",
  signal_type: "rate_limit_pain" | "sustained_spend" | "security_intent" | "region_residency" | "routing_failures",
  score: 0-100,
  account_id: <internal UUID>,
  company_domain: "example.com",
  company_name: "Example, Inc" (if we have it),
  plan_tier: "free"|"pro"|"team"|"enterprise" (self-serve tiers),
  window: "7d"|"14d"|"30d",
  spend_usd_30d: <number>,
  tokens_30d: <number>,
  max_concurrency_7d: <number>,
  rate_limit_429_count_7d: <number>,
  error_rate_5xx_7d: <number>,
  region_top: "us-east"|"eu-west"|...,
  intent_sources: ["pricing_page", "docs_sso", "contact_sales"],
  last_seen_at: <timestamp>,
  links: {
     hubspot_company_url: ...,
     console_account_url: ...,
     support_ticket_url: ... (optional)
  }
}
```

Logan Wright: +1. fwiw Slack message would *not* include the numeric spend/tokens, more like “spend up 3x” / “hit 429s repeatedly” w/ link to HubSpot.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Thanks. Big picture: keep this strictly company/account-level. No user-level identifiers, no request payloads, no IPs, no email addresses.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Specifics:
- `company_domain` is ok.
- `company_name` ok if it’s already in our CRM context.
- `account_id` ok internally, but don’t leak internal UUIDs to Slack.
- Avoid raw counts where it’s not needed for action. For Slack, qualitative bands are better.

Marcus Lin: Agree w/ Aisha. Also: numeric `spend_usd_30d` is sensitive business data. If it lands in HubSpot, make sure permissions are restricted (Sales/RevOps only) and we’re not auto-posting it into public-ish Slack channels.

David Kim: On HubSpot side we can store as custom properties and restrict view/edit by team. Timeline events are visible to many by default though; we should be careful what we put in the event body vs properties.

Isabelle Laurent: +1 — we’ve had issues where timeline events get screen-shared. Would prefer timeline event copy be “High intent signal: sustained usage growth” and numbers only in properties (or not at all).

Nadia Rahman: Re: schema — counts come from aggregated tables keyed by `account_id`. We never store end-user emails in telemetry anyway. But “contact_sales” event could include a typed email field today (from the webform). We should explicitly *not* forward that into the signal event.

Naomi Feldman: Good catch. For `intent_sources` we can just emit `contact_sales=true` without details.

Benji Okafor: For “sensitive accounts” — we already have an internal flag `account_sensitivity = standard|restricted` (fed/healthcare/known regulated). Proposal: if restricted, suppress Slack notifications entirely and only write to HubSpot with an internal note + assign to AE/CSM per routing.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. Add: if `restricted`, also avoid including `company_domain` in Slack even if you decide to notify (I’d rather we just suppress). Keep it to “restricted account triggered signal” w/ link that requires auth.

Logan Wright: Works. Implementation-wise, Slack notifier can check `account_sensitivity` and short-circuit.

Marcus Lin: Another item: `region_top` could be fine, but don’t include precise geolocation beyond region. No IP-derived anything.

Nadia Rahman: Region is from deployment config / routing region, not IP. But we can label it as “requested/served region”.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Perfect.

David Kim: Action item for me: we should avoid putting a JSON blob with everything in the timeline event body. HubSpot timelines become messy + hard to permission. Better: minimal timeline text + key/value properties on company record.

Isabelle Laurent: Also dedupe: timeline spam is a security risk (too much exposure). Cooldown windows help.

Naomi Feldman: Got it. Proposed adjustments based on this thread:
1) Remove user-level fields entirely (no email, no user_id, no IP).
2) Slack: no numeric spend/tokens; use bands and link to HubSpot.
3) HubSpot timeline: minimal copy; numbers (if any) as restricted properties.
4) Suppress Slack notifications for `account_sensitivity=restricted`.
5) `contact_sales` intent only as boolean/source tag (no form contents).

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1 to all. Add one more: retention. Signal events stored in our pipeline should have a defined retention (e.g., 90d) unless there’s a business need. HubSpot will retain longer; keep only what’s necessary there.

Marcus Lin: +1. If you need longer for KPI analysis, do it in aggregated form (counts per week) without identifiers.

Logan Wright: For pipeline tables we can set retention to 90d on the raw signal events table, and separately maintain an aggregate for dashboards (no domain, just segment). I’ll sync with Mei.

Naomi Feldman: Sounds good. Aisha/Marcus — is this a “ship it” given changes above?

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes, ship with those constraints. Please tag me on the final field list PR/Confluence doc so we have an audit trail.

Marcus Lin: Approved from me as well, contingent on Slack suppression for restricted + no numeric spend in Slack.

Naomi Feldman: Awesome. I’ll update the schema + notify Eng. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
